jobs.description: Work Your Magic with us!Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That's why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us.Everything we do in Electronics is to help us deliver on our purpose of being the company behind the companies, advancing digital living. We are dedicated to being the trusted supplier of high-tech materials, services and specialty chemicals for the electronics, automotive and cosmetics industries. We foster a global collaborative organization made up of individuals who have the passion to win, obsess about the customer, are relentlessly curious and act with urgency. Together, we push the boundaries of science to make more possible for our customers.Your roleHelp bring next-generation formulation materials to scale by building quality and reliability into products and processes from development through high-volume manufacturing. You’ll ensure disciplined analytics and effective process controls are in place to monitor product and process health. As a voice of the customer, you’ll help cross-functional teams resolve issues quickly, assess deviations rigorously, and minimize customer impact. You’ll lead structured problem solving and effective corrective and preventive actions, while helping teams identify abnormal events and sources of variation. You’ll strengthen a proactive quality culture, contribute to site audits, and champion improvements that keep pace with semiconductor customers’ needs. You’ll collaborate across sites and time zones, with travel to global manufacturing locations and, when needed, customer sites.Who you are- You have a bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, Materials Science, or another technical discipline.- You bring at least eight years of experience in chemical manufacturing, process or control engineering, analytical chemistry, and/or semiconductor fabrication.- You communicate excellently in written and spoken English.- You have a safety- and quality-focused approach to process controls, risk assessment, and reducing variation; semiconductor industry experience, particularly in fab process engineering, is an advantage.- You have working knowledge of SPC and statistical methods such as t-tests, ANOVA, and univariate or multivariate modeling.- You have experience with quality and problem-solving methods such as 5 Whys, segmentation, model-based problem solving, FMEAs, CAPA, change management, continuous improvement, and document control.- You are comfortable with data and process-improvement tools such as JMP, Palantir Foundry, Tableau, Python, JSL, or SAP; experience with data automation, digitization, and ISO 9001 quality systems is valued.- You build strong cross-functional relationships, motivate others, and stay organized, attentive to detail, and resilient through ambiguity; auditor or Six Sigma certification and additional languages are a plus.What we offer: We are curious minds that come from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We believe that this variety drives excellence and innovation, strengthening our ability to lead in science and technology. We are committed to creating access and opportunities for all to develop and grow at your own pace. Join us in building a culture of inclusion and belonging that impacts millions and empowers everyone to work their magic and champion human progress!Apply now and become a part of a team that is dedicated to Sparking Discovery and Elevating Humanity!

Research Associate (m/f/d), EG 14 TV-H, fixed-term, full-time (currently 40 hours per week)Application deadline:20.11.2026Date of hire:01.01.2027vacancy number:39545The post is initially limited until 31 December 2028 as part of the ‘DyNaMo’ project, in accordance with its duration (academic qualification position pursuant to § 2 WissZeitVG).  An extension of the employment is planned. The opportunity to obtain a habilitation degree is given.The Intelligent Embedded Systems (IES) group conducts research in the area of fundamentals and applications of methods in data analysis, machine learning (e.g. deep learning, active learning) and artificial intelligence. In the focus of basic research are, for example, self-learning and self-organizing systems, methods of collaborative and active learning, methods of transfer learning, and techniques for real-time analysis of time series. Applied research focuses on the fields of energy systems, automotive (autonomous driving) and experimental physics/materials. The IES group currently employs around 20 researchers in the above areas.Your tasks:- Methods for perceiving cyclists’ behaviour by using machine learning techniques (in particular deep learning approaches) based on data from vehicle sensors (e.g. camera and LiDAR data).- Cross-labelling approaches for the highly automated annotation of cyclists’ behaviour data, i.e. transferring ‘labels’ from, for example, camera data to LiDAR data.- Methods for integrating information from models trained on different data modalities and evaluating the resulting information gain.- Planning and conducting measurement campaigns in the form of laboratory experiments as well as field experiments.- Research within the DyNaMo project.- Contributing to the group’s general tasks.Requirements:- A PhD and a completed university degree in Computer Science or a closely related field- Excellent knowledge in perception and computer vision.- Very good fundamental knowledge in machine learning and data analysis.- A successful academic career with high-impact publications in the relevant fields.- Experience in external fundraising (e.g. LOEWE, BMFTR, DFG).- Experience in programming, particularly in Python, but also in other programming languages.- Good knowledge of AI tools, e.g. PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, Pandas, OpenCV and NumPy.- A structured approach to work that enables you to lead a team.- A keen interest in the challenges posed by machine learning applications in the field of automated driving.- An independent and goal-oriented approach to work, and a passion for scientific research.- Very good written and spoken German and English (at least B2 level in each).- A driving licence valid in Germany for passenger cars.The following conditions are advantageous- Experience in organisation and coordination (e.g. project management, team leadership).- Experience in supervising PhD students, e.g. when they write publications.As a member of staff in the Intelligent Embedded Systems group:- You will lead a small but highly motivated team,- you will have the opportunity to attend conferences, summer schools, and various professional development programmes (e.g. the opportunity to obtain a habilitation degree),- you will have access to your own, very large Slurm-based compute cluster (CPU and GPU),- you will have access to your own, state-of-the-art test vehicle (a car equipped with a camera, LiDAR and radar),- you will be able to develop new methods for use in practical applications.In case of any questions ask Prof. Dr. B. Sick, bsick(at)uni-kassel.de

Your applicationPlease submit a cover letter describing your motivation and relevant research experience, a CV, academic certificates/transcripts, and contact details of two referees via the UMG application portal. Please indicate relevant programming projects or publications where applicable.We look forward to receiving your application!Travel and application expenses cannot be reimbursed.Your tasks•  Design and perform multielectrode in vivo electrophysiological recordings from the inferior colliculus of the Mongolian gerbil.•  Develop and validate computational and data-driven models of auditory information processing and optogenetically evoked neural responses.•  Integrate experimental measurements into a digital-twin framework and assess model generalization, uncertainty and biological plausibility.•  Design and optimize sound-processing algorithms that map acoustic signals to spatial and temporal optical stimulation patterns, and benchmark their performance in vivo and in silico.•  Collaborate with experimental neuroscientists and engineers; present and publish scientific findings and contribute to interdisciplinary project meetings.Your qualifications•  Completed MSc or equivalent in neuroscience, biomedical/electrical engineering, biology, physics or a related field.•  Enthusiasm for in vivo electrophysiology. No prior in vivo experience is required; full training in electrophysiological techniques will be provided.•  Good programming skills (preferably MATLAB/Python) and experience in signal processing, scientific computing or machine learning.•  Strong analytical skills, curiosity about biological systems and enthusiasm for developing experimental and computational research.•  Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary, international team; very good written and spoken English.•  Knowledge of auditory neuroscience, PyTorch/JAX or computational neuroprosthetics is an advantage but not a prerequisite.We offer•  A scientifically ambitious PhD project at the interface of in vivo electrophysiology, computational modeling and optogenetic neurotechnology for future hearing restoration.•  Close interaction with teams at IAN and EKFZ-OT developing optical cochlear implants, with access to complementary experimental, computational and engineering expertise.•  An internationally connected Göttingen Campus research environment, opportunities for doctoral training at the Göttingen Graduate Center for Neuroscience, Biophysics and Molecular Biosciences.•  Support for scientific publications, professional development and participation in collaborative research networks and training academies.•  Employment and social benefits in accordance with the applicable TV-L regulations; final contract conditions to be specified.This PhD project is funded by CAIMed (Lower Saxony Center for AI and Causal Methods in Medicine) and will contribute to the Göttingen program developing optical cochlear implants for future hearing restoration.The goal is to establish an experimentally grounded digital twin of the auditory system and use it to generate, optimize, and benchmark sound-coding strategies for optogenetic stimulation of the auditory nerve. Combining in vivo electrophysiology, computational neuroscience, and generative modeling, the project investigates how acoustic signals can be transformed into spatiotenporal light patterns for stimulation via the optical cochlear implant under development at IAN and EKFZ-OT.

jobs.description: About usAirbus ist Pionier einer nachhaltigen Luft- und Raumfahrt für eine sichere und vereinte Welt. Das Unternehmen arbeitet ständig an Innovationen für effiziente und technologisch fortschrittliche Lösungen in den Bereichen Luft- und Raumfahrt, Verteidigung sowie vernetzte Dienstleistungen. Airbus bietet moderne und treibstoffeffiziente Verkehrsflugzeuge sowie dazugehörige Dienstleistungen an. Airbus ist auch führend in Europa im Bereich Verteidigung und Sicherheit und eines der größten Raumfahrtunternehmen der Welt. Im Bereich Hubschrauber stellt Airbus die weltweit effizientesten Lösungen und Dienstleistungen für zivile und militärische Hubschrauber bereit.Job descriptionAre you eager to pioneer cutting-edge simulation technologies for the future of sustainable aviation?In order to support the intersection of Aerospace Engineering and Software Development , Airbus is looking for aSoftware Development Engineer for Flight Physics Capabilities / Loads & Aeroelastics(d/f/m)About Us & LocationsThe Flight Physics domain is at the core of aircraft architecture and system integration. Within our team, we develop, maintain, and advance our internal in-house simulation software for aircraft loads & aeroelastics.You will ideally be working in Hamburg, the largest production site for civil aircraft. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe offers unique perks, such as the option to commute by ferry, allowing you to experience the special flair of Hamburg where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets maritime legacy.As our team operates across international engineering hubs, Bremen (Germany) and Filton (UK) are also possible locations for this role. Across all sites, close collaboration and team spirit are central to how we work, which is why regular on-site presence at your chosen location is required.Your MissionYou will be a key developer for our internal loads simulation software. In this role, you will bridge the gap between flight physics domain knowledge and software engineering. You will participate in all phases of the software lifecycle—from defining simulation requirements and architectural design to implementation, automated testing, and deployment. Your code will directly enable engineering teams across Airbus to calculate and evaluate aircraft loads accurately and efficiently.Our Benefits for You- Fair Compensation & Extras: Attractive remuneration and individual additional benefits, such as company pension schemes, mobility offers (e.g., bike leasing), or corporate discounts with partner companies in accordance with our current guidelines.- Time for You (and Your Loved Ones): 30 days of annual leave based on our collective agreement (35-hour week); work-life balance through flexible working hours (flextime), mobile working, part-time options, job sharing, and sabbatical opportunities.- Growth Made Easy: Excellent professional development opportunities and international, group-wide career perspectives.- Feel Good at Work: On-site company doctor; comprehensive health programs (sports courses, preventive care, etc.), canteen and cafeteria, and local childcare facilities at selected locations.- Diversity Connects: Work in a diverse environment with more than 140 nationalities, where exchange, mutual support, and inclusion are part of our DNA.Your tasks and responsibilities- In-House Simulation Tool Development: Design, code, test, deploy, and continuously enhance our internal simulation software dedicated to aircraft loads and aeroelastics.- Algorithm & Architecture Design: Implement advanced numerical methods and physical models into clean, high-performance, and modular code.- Requirements Translation: Collaborate closely with Flight Physics loads engineers to translate complex aerodynamic and structural load requirements into efficient software algorithms.- User Support & Tool Maintenance: Provide technical support to internal engineering users, troubleshoot simulation issues, and optimize software performance and usability based on user feedback.- Engineering Best Practices: Apply modern software engineering standards, including peer code reviews, CI/CD, version control, and comprehensive testing to ensure simulation accuracy and code reliability.Desired skills and qualifications- Domain Background: Degree in Aerospace Engineering, Aeronautics, Computational Engineering, Physics, or a related field with a solid understanding of flight physics, aircraft loads, or structural mechanics.- Hands-on Programming Skills: Strong coding abilities and solid experience in object-oriented programming (OOP) using Python, C++, or C#.- Systems & Infrastructure: Experience working in Linux environments. Practical knowledge of High-Performance Computing (HPC), parallel computing, or aeroelastic simulation workflows is a major advantage.- Software Engineering Practice: Solid foundation in modern development workflows, including Git/version control, unit testing, and CI/CD practices.- Problem-Solving & Mindset: A passion for translating physical engineering problems into robust, automated software tools.- Communication & Team Spirit: Excellent communication skills in English, good Level of German speaking with an open, collaborative approach to working in an international engineering team.Not a 100% match?
